dedupe_keys.name: shock propagation in the international multilayer food production network csh vienna code

description: This repository holds the Python code of the Complexity Science Hub Vienna study of how production shocks spread through the international multilayer food-production network, written for the paper by Laber, Klimek, Bruckner, Yang and Thurner on global food availability after the Ukraine war. The script shock-complete.py simulates a worst case of a total production loss of all products at once, and shock-individual.py one product at a time; two further scripts compute the relative loss of availability per country against an unshocked baseline. The model is global, at country and product level, and is built on trade, production and usage data for the single year 2013 taken from the FABIO food and agriculture biomass input-output database. Access is a public GitHub repository of scripts; the repository names no licence, so reuse terms are unclear although it is free to read. Caveats: the base year is 2013, the input data must be obtained separately, and the code is a research artefact without releases or documentation beyond the README. It supports cascading failure and network flow analysis of food supply chains and resilience scenarios for food security. Related record: data-fabio-food-agriculture-biomass-input-output supplies the input tables.
